item: Memory gate before staging, safe read-only URIs, encrypted newsletter drop without VACUUM
summary: Follow-up to the encrypted merge memory gate (#1328). The legacy and volume restores (so the import queue) check memory before staging. Four hand-built file: URIs go through one percent-encoding helper (a ? or # in a directory name opened another path read-write). The encrypted newsletter-excluded backup copy is no longer VACUUMed (366 MB peak RSS on 60,000 articles, in memory under SQLCipher): it deletes with secure_delete, merges the search index (deleted words survived VACUUM and the export, plain path included) and rewrites the survivors into a fresh keyed file (87 MB), key bound and never in SQL text, every cipher setting copied and read back, any failure keeps the secure-delete result and says which path ran. The index merge and the rewrite each ask for their room on the copy itself. Each guard has a test that fails without it (the free pages' zeroing is tested on a plaintext twin, the encrypted build having no page view). NEWSLETTERS-EXCLUDED BACKUPS MADE BEFORE THIS VERSION still carry the excluded newsletters' search-index entries: the words AND their positions (the index is FTS5 detail=full, so the order of a newsletter's lower-cased words can be read back from the file once decrypted; the original casing, punctuation and the text itself are not there). Making a new backup drops them. There is no in-app prompt.
